newsitem.title: USA: Neurogen obesity drug safe in Phase Ib.
newsitem.headline: Neurogen obesity drug safe in Phase Ib.

text.p: Neurogen Corp said on Thursday that Phase Ib human clinical studies of NGD 95-1, the new anti-obesity drug it is co-developing with Pfizer Inc showed the drug to be safe and well tolerated across a broad dose range.
The trial tested the drug's safety and pharmacokinetic profile over 14 days of multiple dose administration to overweight, but otherwise healthy, male and female volunteers.
"As we pass the clinical development baton to Pfizer, we are both very satisfied with the Phase I results," said Harry Penner, Neurogen's president and CEO in a press release.
"Both companies are looking forward to evaluating the efficacy of the compound in Phase II placebo-controlled weight loss studies."
NGD 95-1 is an orally active small molecule antagonist of neuropeptide Y (NPY) receptors.
NPY, a chemical messenger in the brain, is strongly linked to appetite and is thought to be the most potent known stimulator of eating in animals.
Neurogen said that it has demonstrated in animal studies that NGD 95-1 blocks NPY-induced feeding, and in a three week study, it significantly reduced weight gain in normal rats.
